cells.tense: Right now the inquiry is steady and the shares on the pan are landing where they belong.
cells.act: build the change by persistent work
cells.ask: An hour a day this week, keep building the change your work already points at — the small persistent kind, no announcement, nothing stopped until it holds.
cells.core:
Your method is doing what it is for. You inquire carefully, and the care reaches the shares themselves — the hours, the attention, what each person has to carry — so what each thing deserves comes out close to right. Nothing gets overridden. Nobody gets quietly shortchanged. You can feel the difference between a good call and a rushed one, and you are making the good ones.
When a structural change is genuinely called for, put your weight behind it and keep going one real inch at a time. The change you make over the next weeks is the kind that holds because it got built rather than announced. The slower pace is not a problem to fix. It is the reason the thing will still be standing after you step away from it.

cells.tense: Your mind is already ruling on the next case, running past what has happened and cannot yet be written in.
cells.act: drop one condition you set and take the step
cells.ask: Let one condition go — the strict one that has kept the next move stalled — and make the move this week with that condition unmet.
cells.core:
Where you inquire and rule, the judging has gotten out past the material. You are deciding cases before the facts have landed, and every new situation is being answered by a verdict you wrote earlier. The fairness you are reaching for is real. It has just stopped waiting for the weight to actually drop onto the pan.
One of the conditions you have laid on the next move can come off. You know which — the requirement so strict that nothing clears it, so nothing gets finished. Do the thing with that condition unmet, and let what you have already built be enough to close the rest out. Surrender is not defeat here, and the step goes through.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that has already closed behind you, and your method is still waiting for it to open.
cells.act: weigh what it costs them against what it gives
cells.ask: A feeling you have kept unresolved about somebody: weigh what carrying it draws out of them and what it yields you, make the call a single time, and stand by the call.
cells.core:
The weighing has stalled. Where you used to make careful calls and settle them, you now leave them sitting on the pan until the moment has gone. You are still reasonable — you can see every side — but seeing every side has turned into a way of not choosing one, and your method sits unused while you wait.
Take a single feeling you have been carrying about someone and judge it fairly. Ask what carrying it does to them, and what it does for you. Whatever answer arrives, that is the answer, not one more question. Acting on the call straight away is not required. Making it and standing by it is the whole ask. One feeling is enough. The scales are not broken; they have gone quiet.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where your method is still quietly deciding what is fair.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: After the next piece of work you finish, sit a few minutes and wonder what comes after — the wondering, not the plan — then walk one small step toward it.
cells.core:
You go on measuring, and the measuring is yours, but whether the balance you keep is anyone's in particular is a question you have not been asking. You keep things square out of habit and call it just how you are. The squareness is not in question. What is unattributed is the sense that something right is being built here, by someone.
There is a next step you have not let yourself picture, and it is not for lack of ideas. It is that when you finish, you set the tools down and go straight to the next finished item without feeling forward. Sit with work you have genuinely completed, let a picture of what comes next rise, and go toward it small. An inch counts. Wondering is not a betrayal of rigor; it is what the rigor was for.
